articleTitle: Real-time rule based resource allocation in naval command and control
publicationTitle: IEE Colloquium on Rule-Based Systems for Real-Time Planning and Control
abstract: It is argued that automation can be provided in the area of reactive resource allocation on a worship and is a more straightforward problem than initially conceived. The output of such a system, be it fully automated or performed by men with decision support, is capable of being evaluated and compared with human performance alone, both in terms of effectiveness in countering the threat, and for speed of response. A spin-off from the implementation of a resource allocation prototype may be its value as a training aid, enabling experiential learning and student-paced development of expertise at the same time as the development of trust and confidence in the system. In this form it could also provide a 'what if' test bed on which principal warfare officers could explore variations of tactics prior to a mission.<<ETX xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">></ETX>

articleTitle: Safety critical aspects of real-time expert systems
publicationTitle: IEE Colloquium on Rule-Based Systems for Real-Time Planning and Control
abstract: The paper concerns a research programme which attempts to draw together different sectors involved in safety-critical systems. The different sectors have different approaches, and the aim is to explore the differences so as to facilitate harmonisation. The sector involved include those of AI and software engineering. A further aim is to develop new software techniques by the comparison and contrasting of existing ones.<<ETX xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">></ETX>

articleTitle: Object-oriented programming languages for real-time rule-based systems: a practical evaluation
publicationTitle: IEE Colloquium on Rule-Based Systems for Real-Time Planning and Control
abstract: This paper outlines the results of a project concerned with investigating engineering techniques for real-time expert systems, and includes work concerned with parallel processing, formal specification, quality assurance and safety-critical systems. The authors seek to evalutate the utility of object-oriented programming languages for implementing an experimental real-time blackboard expert system for data fusion in naval command and control systems. The evaluation has taken the form of implementing the data-fusion model in two object-oriented programming languages, Smalltalk-80 and Lingo, and two conventional languages, Ada and C. The implementations are compared with regard to quantitative run-time performance and qualitative software engineering properties.<<ETX xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">></ETX>

articleTitle: Reactive scheduling for hard real time systems
publicationTitle: IEE Colloquium on Rule-Based Systems for Real-Time Planning and Control
abstract: Constraint maintenance is a well-known and an effective general problem-solving strategy in AI. This approach has been successful in developing a reactive scheduler for VLSI plant operation. A constraint net models the real world problem and this net can be updated at little cost with an immediate check on the feasibility of the schedule. The favourable attributes of this approach for application in real time systems are its flexibility in handling dynamic scheduling aspects, minimal run time cost in establishing revised schedules, the constant availability of a feasible schedule for immediate use and the maintenance of the whole set of solutions. The paper discusses the practical issues both in relation to application of the technique in real time control and its implementation in hard real time systems. The application of the technique to real-time control focusses on the relationship of the primitives of the scheduler to typical high-level real-time constraints, as well as the extent to which the technique may be applicable. The paper also examines the incorporation of the scheduler in a real-time embedded system. When an infeasible schedule occurs a rule-based strategy is invoked to recover the feasible one. This implies the selective shedding of scheduled tasks with the probable consequences of an orderly shutdown of the affected area of the plant by the real-time system.<<ETX xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">></ETX>

articleTitle: The practical application of rule and knowledge based system techniques to industrial processes
publicationTitle: IEE Colloquium on Rule-Based Systems for Real-Time Planning and Control
abstract: This paper concerns the application of rule and knowledge based techniques to the control and optimisation of industrial processes. It is based on work initiated by Blue Circle plc for the optimisation of the control of cement kilns. This work has resulted in the development of a commercial product, known as LINKman, which has been installed successfully in twenty three plants worldwide where it achieves substantial savings in fuel and improvements in quality. This paper looks at the techniques and discusses some of the practical issues involved in their application.<<ETX xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">></ETX>

articleTitle: The role of formal specification in rule-based real-time AI
publicationTitle: IEE Colloquium on Rule-Based Systems for Real-Time Planning and Control
abstract: This paper describes the role of formal specification in the development of AI systems: it is seen as an important step in the development of reliable real-time AI systems. It discusses some of the issues involved in formal specification and their relationship to current practise and theory. Three completed specifications are described. The paper describes the use of formal methods in the development of AI interpreters and relates formal methods at this level to work in knowledge representation. The role of formal specification in the modelling of experimental systems is also discussed.<<ETX xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">></ETX>
